clue.text: Dry and dull, first off

indicators.note: first off asks for the opening letter of the word for dull to be dropped

parts.note: dull in the sense of stupid, lacking intelligence

explanation.surface: A grumble about a boring, parched day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' removes the B from BRAINLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry spell is one with no precipitation at all, so dry weather is rain-free.

clue.text: Why you are, before tea, announced in tent

indicators.note: announced means everything is spoken aloud and the letters are taken from the sounds

parts.note: why, you and are sound like the letters Y, U and R, and tea following them sounds like T

explanation.surface: Someone asks a camper why they are in the tent before teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' turns the spoken words into letter sounds: Y, U, R and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A yurt is a round felt-covered dwelling of Central Asian nomads, a kind of portable shelter.

clue.text: Stupidly heat neon or other gas

indicators.note: stupidly signals that these letters are to be jumbled carelessly into a new order

parts.note: NE is the chemical symbol for neon

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly heats a neon tube or some other gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupidly' rearranges HEAT plus NE; 'other' marks it as a gas besides neon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a colourless hydrocarbon found in natural gas, another gas besides neon.

clue.text: Awful regal family's on top in this tragedy

indicators.note: on top places the family word above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: kin means one's family or relations

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters of the word regal are put in a dreadful mess

explanation.surface: A tragedy in which a dreadful royal family dominates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' is the anagram signal and 'on top' places the family first in the down light; the surface describes the play itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about an old monarch and his daughters is one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: Shut up about learner, one absorbed in text

indicators.note: about means the word for shut up goes around the other letters

parts.note: shut up meaning confined, as prisoners are interned
L is the learner driver's plate
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tutor tells a learner to be quiet, while someone is engrossed in reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L and I inside INTERNED. 'Shut up' looks like a rude command but means imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Words written between the lines of a manuscript are taken into the text itself.

clue.text: Cane despicable chap — beat on bottom

indicators.note: on bottom places the beating word below the other in this down entry

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person
to tan someone's hide is to thrash them

explanation.surface: Using a cane on a rotten fellow's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on bottom' looks like part of the corporal punishment but places TAN under RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is the climbing palm whose stems are used as canes and for furniture.

clue.text: French that's grasped by dull artist's model

indicators.note: grasped by means the French word is held inside the word for dull

parts.note: matte means dull, without sheen
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A French sculptor's model is held by a dull artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasped by' is the container signal; 'artist's model' suggests a person posing, but here it is a small sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A maquette is a small preliminary sculpture, a sculptor's model for a larger work.

clue.text: Join forces with soldiers wanting leader on border

indicators.note: on places the reduced soldiers word above the other in this down entry
wanting leader means the word for soldiers loses its first letter

parts.note: men means soldiers, troops in the ranks
a list is an old word for a border or selvage of cloth

explanation.surface: Soldiers without a commander join up along a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting leader' strips M from MEN to leave EN; 'on' puts it above LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for the armed forces, the military being the forces joined.

clue.text: Greek or Roman one found in island heading north

indicators.note: heading means the island comes before the direction
found in means the numeral sits inside the island

parts.note: Iona is a Hebridean island off western Scotland
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A classical figure, Greek or Roman, is discovered on an island while travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek or Roman' looks like the definition, but 'Roman one' gives I; 'found in' puts it in IONA, and 'heading' sets that before N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionians were one of the ancient Hellenic peoples, so the word describes something from Greece.

clue.text: Ammunition centre for platoon, say

indicators.note: centre means the letters are taken from the very middle of the word ammunition

explanation.surface: An ammunition depot serving an infantry platoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is an example of a military subdivision or formation.

clue.text: Short charge by furry animal turning quite quickly

indicators.note: short means the charging word loses its last letter

parts.note: to allege is to charge or accuse

indicators.note: turning means the animal's name is read backwards

parts.note: an otter is a furry river mammal

explanation.surface: A brief attack by a furry creature that wheels round rather fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts ALLEGE to ALLEG; 'turning' gives RETTO from OTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning moderately brisk, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Make safe and secure at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters of secure are jumbled

explanation.surface: Making a vessel safe and fastening it while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges SECURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone from danger is to bring them to safety, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Huge concern, husband being missing, ruined match

indicators.note: being missing means the husband's letter is taken out of the pool
ruined means the remaining letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A wife's great worry as a missing husband wrecks a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H out of HUGE CONCERN ('being missing') and 'ruined' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Congruence is agreement or correspondence, as when two things match exactly.

clue.text: Relieving pressure, going outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for going sits around the pressure letter

parts.note: going as in going cheap, on sale
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Easing the pressure by stepping outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps SELLING round P. Relieving here means taking over a turn of duty; in cricket a bowler is rested this way.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell someone is to take a turn at their work so that they can rest.

clue.text: Divers, after second, wet?

indicators.note: after means the wet word follows the second letter

parts.note: wet means not dry, playfully written as un-dry

explanation.surface: Scuba divers, having surfaced a moment later, are wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like underwater swimmers but is the old adjective meaning various. The question mark flags UNDRY as an invented word for wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an archaic adjective meaning several or various, the same as miscellaneous.

clue.text: Meetings one ruins, being out of order

indicators.note: being out of order means the letters of the two words are disarranged

explanation.surface: A gathering that one person spoils by behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out of order' rearranges ONE RUINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings of people coming together again after time apart, such as old classmates.

clue.text: Finally agreed bowling area's reason to halt cricket

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word agreed is used

parts.note: a rink is a stretch of a bowling green, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A bowls club at last agrees a reason to stop the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket matches pause for scheduled refreshment breaks; 'bowling' here means lawn bowls, not cricket bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshment intervals are a recognised stoppage in a cricket match.

clue.text: Jumper found on beach, also key left nearby?

indicators.note: found on beach suggests the pieces are lying within the sea's edge, so they go inside it

parts.note: the sea is what lies nearby when one is on the shore
and means also, in addition
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: A jumping creature on the shore, plus a key someone left there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a sweater but means a leaping creature; 'found on beach' is the container signal, the sea being what lies nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand flea is a small crustacean that leaps about on the shore, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: Little change once in a definitive work abridged for user

indicators.note: in means the old penny goes inside the other letters
abridged means the reference book's name is cut short

parts.note: a dictionary is the authoritative work on what words mean
D was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A dictionary abridged by someone who once took a small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' gives the common shortened form of the reference book's name; 'in' is the container signal, and D was an old British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user is someone dependent on a substance, the slang sense of user.

clue.text: Comprehensive in which a couple of learners do run amok

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, and a couple of them makes two

indicators.note: amok means running wild, so the letters of do run are scattered

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school where a pair of learner drivers go wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amok' rearranges DO RUN into ROUND. 'Comprehensive' looks like a British state school but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that covers every aspect, like a versatile player, is broad in scope.

clue.text: Endlessly delayed travelling through part of EU

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for delayed loses its final letter

parts.note: late means delayed
via means by way of, passing through

explanation.surface: A long-delayed journey across a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims LATE to LAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic country that joined the European Union in 2004 is one of its member states.

clue.text: Sweet girl, initially sound as a bell, becoming pale

parts.note: Sweet Fanny Adams, a Victorian murder victim whose name became slang for nothing, gives the initials FA
a ding is the sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: A lovely girl who began perfectly healthy is turning wan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy but is DING. 'Sweet FA' is British slang for nothing at all, from Fanny Adams.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing colour or brightness gradually, like wan cheeks or a dimming light.

clue.text: Work out, in shape

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: calculating a sum, and a person's bodily outline.

clue.text: Employing number in East before the revolt

indicators.note: before places the compass letter ahead of the rest

parts.note: a rising is a revolt or uprising

explanation.surface: Recruiting a number of people in the East before an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Administering an anaesthetic gas to a patient is using a substance that deadens feeling.

clue.text: Facility for communication either way in show, if I want

indicators.note: either way means the letters can be found reading forwards in show, if I and backwards in if I want
in means the letters lie inside the words show, if I

explanation.surface: Someone offers to demonstrate a communication service if they wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes the letters from 'show, if I'; 'either way' adds that the same letters also lie backwards in 'if I want'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless internet access is a facility that lets devices connect and exchange messages.

clue.text: Set up regulation about drug producing mark on skin

indicators.note: set up means the whole is turned upwards in this down entry, read from bottom to top
about means the regulation word goes around the drug letter

parts.note: a law is a regulation
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug regulation is framed that leaves a scar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E in LAW; 'Set up' turns LAEW upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ridge on the skin left by a whip or blow is a welt.

clue.text: Team leader filmed, that's full of beans, perhaps

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word team

parts.note: a scene that is filmed is in the can

explanation.surface: A team captain is filmed being full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of beans' suggests lively, but it is literal: a container of baked beans.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal food container is something that may be literally packed with beans.

clue.text: Mad Hatter and neighbours at table are menacing

definitions.note: the plural verb phrase matches the answer as a plural present-tense verb

indicators.note: mad signals that the letters are put in a crazy new order

parts.note: N and E, north and east, are adjacent partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter and fellow guests at the tea party look menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges HATTER plus NE; the surface evokes Alice's tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace is to intimidate or warn of harm, a direct synonym.
